record.file_problem: Repo README and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports outcomes from residual-direction ablation, but describes an optimized pipeline with selected layers and KL-guided search rather than a direct reproduction of the original intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports harmful-refusal outcomes and a KL result after ablation. Values used to choose layers, strengths, directions, or prompts are not recorded as findings. The README also describes baked weights but does not report an evaluation result specifically for the baked checkpoint.
record.test_reason: The README reports harmful refusal rates before and after difference-in-means residual-direction ablation on Qwen2.5 models. That bears on V1. The method adds KL-guided Optuna search over the direction layer, strength α and layer band, so it is a variant rather than a replication.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say ablation reliably removes hard refusals, keyword metrics greatly overstate success, and some refusals resist a linear edit. They regard ~50% judged compliance as a useful result and stress honest LLM-judge evaluation. They do not specifically urge evaluating capability damage beyond KL.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes harmful-minus-harmless difference-of-means extraction and residual projection, but adds KL-guided optimization over direction, strength, and selected layers; it also offers subspace extraction and weight orthogonalization.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says results depend on the refusal metric and judge: keyword refusal can read 0.0 while an LLM judge scores true compliance at approximately 0.49. It also says search-set difficulty, soft-refusal detection, generation length, and selection by judged ASR affect the reported outcome.
record.problems: README-reported results only; no uncertainty estimates or controls are reported. The stated mean KL is a proxy rather than a direct general-capability evaluation. The 1.5B results do not identify the exact direction count, layer selection, prompt-set size, or LLM judge.

record.verdict_notes: This is a README of a toolkit, not a study. No uncertainty or controls are reported, and code and notebooks were not read. The V4 'supports' guess was dropped because the README gives an assertion, not a test. The 0.5B 'verified result' is likely the search's own selected-config output under a keyword metric.

versions.untested_parts: Adding the direction to induce refusals on harmless requests; direct evaluation of general capabilities beyond the reported KL proxy; whether ablation at every layer and position is required.
The README describes weight orthogonalization and a released checkpoint, but does not report refusal results specifically for a weight-edited model.
Whether jailbreaks suppress the direction, or training against ablation increases robustness.
The README reports redundant or distributed encoding, but does not test affine or cone geometry or compare those descriptions systematically.
Whether harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions are encoded separately.
Transfer across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
How refusal-training choices determine whether a removable direction exists.
Whether the result holds for reasoning models.
